chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (AS) saying: 'Blessed is the man who does not die until he sees a successor from himself.'

key_terms.خَلَف: successor, offspring — one who comes after and takes the place of another; used here for a child or descendant who will continue the line
key_terms.سَعِدَ: became happy / was blessed — a formula expressing felicity for the one in whom a quality is found; the verbal form intensifies the sense of genuine happiness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim say about the blessing of having children before death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kazim (AS) declares that it is a source of happiness and blessing for a person to live long enough to witness their own progeny. This teaching appears in Kitab al-Nikah (Book of Marriage) under the chapter on the resemblance of children to their parents, situating it within Shia jurisprudential discussions of marriage and family continuity. The statement reflects the classical Islamic value of carrying on through righteous offspring, echoing the supplications of the prophets Zachariah and Yahya (Quran 3:38, 19:5) who sought successors to carry on their legacy.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Happiness of a person is that he does not die until he sees a successor from himself’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from a man who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Fortunate is the man who does not die before seeing a successor of his own self.’”
